title: Publish as a validated single commit to the content repository
mechanism: An authenticated owner edits content in a small admin page. The server validates the submission with the same validator the build runs, then writes it through the Git Data API as blobs, a tree, one commit, and one fast-forward-only ref update. The ordinary build deploys the new commit.
invariant: Publishing equals one validated commit to the repository, the ordinary build deploys it, and reverting the commit undoes the publish.
applicability: Applies to small owner-edited content sites whose deployment builds from a Git repository. It does not apply where content must change without a build, where edits are high frequency, or where the host does not build from repository commits.

evidence.observation: A publish touching three documents produced exactly one commit and one build; mutation M3 fails the harness when two changed documents produce more than one commit. A stale base is refused with 409 before the ref update, and the ref PATCH omits force so a non-fast-forward is an error rather than a silent overwrite.
The owner's publish reached the live site on both the apex and pages.dev within roughly 90 seconds, confirming the host builds commits produced by this mechanism.

assumptions.statement: The hosting platform builds and deploys any commit pushed to the tracked branch.
The commit author identity used by the publisher is accepted by the hosting platform as a project contributor.
The request handler signature and environment access follow the host's function model.
A platform key-value binding is available to throttle repeated login attempts.
A central middleware file can gate every authenticated route.
